blacklistabilityReview.evidence: STUSD has a live holder-selective lock-extension and lock-revival control on its sole tracked BSC deployment 0x806dd21af6de051fb811760a5768d04a99160eb9. At BSC block 128510562 (2026-10-19T07:00:40Z; hash 0x718358e2c7285a3dd062c93f608b0fefad7696f04a9cda980b05513805868a95), its immutable wrapper was 0xb4d3c1bb59be7b419af4e10e9b240f425782b22a, with live owner 0x9ab82f8e97bf3202173b92e06e6593f336b76ccf and token MINTER_ROLE assigned to that wrapper. The verified v2.0.1 token and v3.0.1 wrapper runtime exactly matched their deployed code. STUSD._update checks the sender's wrapper lock before ordinary transfers. The owner/operator's wrapWithLock(to,amount,unlockTime) increases the recipient's stored locked amount and can extend its expiry without the recipient's consent. The amount is never cleared when expiry passes: getLockInfo merely returns zero while expired. Sending a new dust locked issuance can therefore revive the historical amount against a pre-existing unlocked holder balance. The current owner address itself demonstrates the state: 5951938122217323694533 raw STUSD balance, an expired stored lock of 10000000000000000000000 until 1764953363, and getLockInfo=(0,0). Nonadmin 0x9896862b7282d4730facd3934e5c13c3a3f28afc currently holds 771000000000000000000 raw units under a lock ending 1797281445; a later issuer mint can extend that same existing balance's lock. The same authority owns upstream sUSDC, is permanently unlocked there, and can mint funding dust using recordReward; that owner-sender call succeeded non-persistently at the pin. There is no claim that a relock transaction was executed. STUSD and its wrapper remain non-proxy contracts with no token-level blacklist or global pause, but their deployed external lock hook already supplies a live holder-targeted intervention path, so Yes applies rather than Possible. Upstream sUSDC remains a separate proxy at 0xad66385c6db496258771b5fd8ac376e3dd0d1536 using implementation 0xe1bf9310f23db3fd05931aa89879d5247bb2a678; it was unpaused and retains holder-lock, forced-transfer and burn functions. The declared USDC lineage is secondary because the direct control decides the verdict. Verified source governs deployed behavior where issuer documentation differs; missing public audit or reserve publications are not used as access-control evidence.
